pull.title: test: fuzz paths that random inputs almost never reach
pull.body:
Based on #1956; only the last three commits are new. Random inputs almost never reach three paths: the retry loop in ECDSA signing, because RFC6979 practically never returns an invalid nonce; the rejection in ECDSA and Schnorr verification when the computed point is infinity; and silent payments output creation for a spend key of minus the output tweak. The first commit signs in the `ecdsa` and `recovery` targets with a nonce function that first returns 0 or a value above n, or fails at a chosen attempt, and checks that signing fails exactly when the nonce function does; `schnorrsig` gets such nonces too, checked only as far as its header documents. The second commit builds the key or signature that makes verification compute infinity, and checks that it is rejected. Both techniques come from @erickcestari's [diffsecp](https://github.com/erickcestari/diffsecp). The third commit, as @Yudis-bit suggested on #1956, sometimes sets the spend key to minus the tweak, checks that output creation fails as documented and that the target's fallback then works, and moves the sent output among the decoys.

With `-seed=1 -runs=20000 -len_control=0`, the retry loop in `ecdsa` and `recovery`, both infinity rejections and the silent payments fallback each run thousands of times; on #1956 all five are 0. Breaking each path on purpose, by stopping at an invalid nonce, accepting at infinity or creating an output for minus the tweak, makes the targets fail.

committer Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1793008664 +0100

test: add libFuzzer harness with ecdsa, recovery and ecdh targets

This is the harness of PR #744, rebased on the current tree. It is
built as one binary, `fuzz`, which picks the target from the FUZZ
environment variable, as Bitcoin Core does. Like the tests, it includes
secp256k1.c, so that targets for internal functions can be added later.
Module targets live in src/modules/<module>/fuzz_impl.h.

The code is updated to the current API (secp256k1_context_static,
SECP256K1_CONTEXT_NONE, secp256k1_ec_seckey_*), uses
secp256k1_memcmp_var, and is C89 clean under the project's warning
flags. The checks are those of #744, with these changes:

- consume_pubkey copies the x coordinate after the prefix byte instead
  of over it.
- The Pubkey(seckey1+seckey2) check accepts seckey1 + seckey2 == 0 mod
  n, where seckey_tweak_add, pubkey_combine and pubkey_tweak_add all
  return 0. It checks that they agree and fail exactly in that case.
- secret_msg and predefined_pubkey are one byte longer, for the NUL: a
  32-byte literal in a 32-byte array fails -Werror with
  -Wunterminated-string-initialization (clang 23, GCC 15).
- The scratch space block is dropped: secp256k1_scratch_space_create
  left the API in 0.6.0.
- A NULL data pointer with size 0 is replaced by a non-NULL one, since
  the targets do arithmetic on it.

committer Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1793008665 +0100

build: add fuzz target to autotools and CMake

The fuzz target is built with --enable-fuzz or -DSECP256K1_BUILD_FUZZ=ON
and is off by default. Like tests, it is compiled with VERIFY, so the
library's internal VERIFY_CHECKs run. It is not a test and does not run
in make check or ctest.

The fuzzing engine is linked from FUZZ_LIBS (SECP256K1_FUZZ_LIBS in
CMake), default -fsanitize=fuzzer, into the fuzz target only.
Instrumentation comes from CFLAGS, e.g.
-fsanitize=fuzzer-no-link,address,undefined. This is the split Bitcoin
Core and OSS-Fuzz use, so that LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE can be passed as
FUZZ_LIBS.

test: add extrakeys and schnorrsig fuzz targets

extrakeys checks that keypair and x-only keys agree with
ec_pubkey_create, that x-only keys round-trip through serialization,
and that keypair_xonly_tweak_add, xonly_pubkey_tweak_add and
xonly_pubkey_tweak_add_check agree. Where the two tweak functions
fail, it checks the cause: a tweak >= n, or one that cancels the even-y
secret key.

schnorrsig checks that signing succeeds and verifies, that sign_custom
with a 32-byte message equals sign32, that a NULL aux_rand32 equals an
all-zero one, that a signature with one bit flipped does not verify,
and that a garbage signature does not verify for a key whose secret
nobody knows.

test: add ellswift fuzz target

It checks that decode(encode(pubkey)) is pubkey, that every 64-byte
string decodes to a key that re-parses, that ellswift_create decodes to
ec_pubkey_create's key, and that both parties of ellswift_xdh get the
same secret. Against 64 arbitrary bytes from the peer, as in BIP324, it
checks that the shared x is the x of our secret key times the decoded
peer key.

test: add musig fuzz target

Each input runs one two-signer session. It checks that nonce_gen
succeeds for a non-zero session_secrand32, that sorted key aggregation
does not depend on the key order, that both partial signatures verify,
that the aggregate signature verifies with schnorrsig_verify, and that
a tampered partial signature does not verify.

test: add silentpayments fuzz target

One sender input pays one recipient. The recipient scans the sent
output among decoys: its own spend key and up to two x-only keys from
the fuzz input. The target checks that the sent output is found, and
that every found output is spendable with the spend key plus its tweak.

create_outputs fails, with one valid input key, only for a spend key
equal to minus the output tweak. There the target retries with the
negated spend key and checks that cause.

committer Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1793008666 +0100

test: check at fuzz startup that valid inputs are accepted

The targets skip inputs that the library rejects as invalid. A library
that rejected every valid secret key, public key or signature would
then pass every run without reaching a check. At startup, the fuzz
binary now aborts unless secret key 1, the generator, a compact ECDSA
signature and, where their modules are enabled, the generator's
x-only key and a partial signature are accepted.

author Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1791125980 +0200
committer Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1793008667 +0100

ci: add libFuzzer job

The job builds with clang, ASan and UBSan, and runs every fuzz target
on an empty corpus for 10000 runs or 20 seconds, whichever comes first.

It passes -len_control=0, so inputs have full length from the first
run. Otherwise libFuzzer lengthens them slowly, and in 10000 runs they
stay under 100 bytes, too short for the musig, ellswift and
silentpayments targets to reach their last checks.

CFLAGS carry -fsanitize=fuzzer-no-link, not -fsanitize=fuzzer: on Linux
clang links the latter as a whole archive, libFuzzer's main included,
into every program it links, which clashes with the main of configure's
checks, the tests and the examples.

committer Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1793008667 +0100

test: tighten fuzz checks after review

fuzz_check_bool checks that a library function returns 0 or 1, as the
API documents.

Public keys parsed from raw input, compressed and uncompressed, must
serialize back to the input, with a hybrid 0x06/0x07 prefix as 0x04.
This catches a parser that accepts a non-canonical encoding.

Raw 32-byte input also checks that ec_pubkey_create and
ec_seckey_verify accept the same secret keys.

The startup check now runs the consume helpers on secret key 1 and the
generator, instead of the library's parsers, which the unit tests
cover. It aborts on a harness bug like the one in #744's
consume_pubkey, which copied the x coordinate over the prefix byte.

Suggested by erickcestari in #1956.

test: reset fuzz context blinding before randomizing

The fuzz context is shared across inputs, and secp256k1_context_randomize
builds on the current blinding. The state used for an input therefore
depended on the inputs run before it, and a crash might not reproduce
from its input alone.

Reset the blinding with a NULL seed first. Suggested by erickcestari.

author Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1791640535 +0200
committer Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1793025825 +0100

test: fuzz signing with nonce functions that force retries

RFC6979 practically never returns a nonce that signing must reject, so
the retry loop in ECDSA signing is not reached by the fuzz targets. The
ecdsa and recovery targets now sign with a nonce function whose first
attempts return 0 or a value >= n, and which can fail at a chosen
attempt; later attempts use RFC6979. They check what the headers
document: attempt counts the previous calls, algo16 is NULL, and
signing fails exactly when the nonce function does. A signature that
is created verifies, or recovers the signing key.

The schnorrsig nonce function has no attempt argument, and the header
does not say what signing does with a nonce of 0 or >= n. The
schnorrsig target signs with a nonce function returning such a nonce, or
failing, and checks only what is documented: a failing nonce function
makes signing fail, a created signature verifies, and the function
receives the x-only key of its secret key.

The technique follows Erick Cestari's diffsecp
(https://github.com/erickcestari/diffsecp, src/targets/ecdsa.c and
src/targets/schnorrsig.c at c9776c4, MIT).

author Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1791640568 +0200
committer Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1793025825 +0100

test: fuzz verification where the computed point is infinity

Random keys and signatures practically never make verification compute
the point at infinity, so its rejection is not reached by the fuzz
targets. The targets now build the key or signature that leads there,
using internal functions only to construct the inputs:

- ecdsa: for a signature (r, s) and message hash z, the key
  Q = -(z/r)*G makes u1*G + u2*Q infinity. No signer holding -z/r can
  produce (r, s), since s would be 0, so verification must fail.
- schnorrsig: for a key with secret d and a fuzzed r, s = e*d makes
  R = s*G - e*P infinity, which BIP-340 verification rejects.

Both constructions follow Erick Cestari's diffsecp
(https://github.com/erickcestari/diffsecp, src/targets/ecdsa.c and
src/targets/schnorrsig.c at c9776c4, MIT).

committer Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1793025826 +0100

test: fuzz silent payments with a spend key of minus the tweak

create_outputs fails for a recipient spend key of -t, where t is the
output tweak, because the output would be infinity. A fuzzed spend key
practically never is -t, so the target's fallback for that case was
never reached. The target now sometimes sets the spend key to -t, built
with internal functions only, and checks that create_outputs returns 0,
as its header documents for an invalid output public key. The fallback
then runs.

It also moves the sent output to a position chosen by the fuzz input,
among the decoys.

Both follow Yudis-bit's suggestion in
https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1956#issuecomment-6099025547.
